cards.explanation: The answer is False. Micah 6:2 says, "For the LORD has a case against His people, and He will argue it against Israel…" The nations aren't in the dock at all. The mountains just get the front-row seats, friends, and nobody asked them to bring cookies.

The answer is how He has wearied them. The LORD says, "Testify against Me how I have wearied you!" (Micah 6:3). He opens the floor and invites His people to speak. I think that's a bold way to start a case, friends, because He's the one asking the questions and still lets them answer.

The answer is Moses and Aaron and Miriam. The LORD says, "I sent Moses before you, as well as Aaron and Miriam." (Micah 6:4). Moses was Israel's leader, Aaron was his brother, and Miriam was their sister (Numbers 26:59). Three siblings walking ahead of a whole nation, which is a lot of family road trip.

The answer is so they'll see the LORD is righteous. He says, "Remember your journey from Shittim to Gilgal, so that you may acknowledge the righteousness of the LORD." (Micah 6:5). Remembering is how they see it. I think that's why He keeps pointing them back to what He already did.

The answer is True. The first offering it wonders about is this: "Should I come to Him with burnt offerings, with year-old calves?" (Micah 6:6). That's where the shopping list starts, friends, and it's about to get a lot bigger. Right after, it asks about "…thousands of rams…" and "…ten thousand rivers of oil?" (Micah 6:7).

The answer is False. After the questions about offerings, the passage says, "He has shown you, O man, what is good." (Micah 6:8). The good thing isn't a secret. It's already been shown, so nobody has to guess or keep adding to the pile.

The answer is justice and mercy and a humble walk with Him. Micah 6:8 says, "And what does the LORD require of you but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?" Three things, friends, and none of them need a shopping trip. I could stamp that on every cookie in the box.
